mainEntity.name: What is the difference between an outdoor fireplace and a fire pit?

acceptedAnswer.text: The main difference lies in their structure, function, and aesthetic. An outdoor fireplace is a more permanent, architectural structure with a chimney that directs smoke upwards, similar to an indoor fireplace. It often serves as a focal point and can be integrated into larger outdoor living spaces. A fire pit, conversely, is typically a lower-profile, open-air structure designed for communal gathering around a contained fire. Fireplaces generally offer more controlled smoke emission and a grander statement, while fire pits provide a more casual, 360-degree experience. Your choice depends on your desired ambiance and space utilization.
acceptedAnswer.description: An outdoor fireplace has a chimney for smoke control and is an architectural focal point, while a fire pit is an open-air, communal fire structure. They offer different aesthetics and functions.
